attempts.raw_response: The fires are largely driven by the draining and burning of peatlands, which are carbon-rich and can smolder underground for weeks, releasing vast amounts of smoke. Despite international pressure and domestic laws, enforcement remains weak, and many plantations operate with impunity. The economic incentives for palm oil, a lucrative global commodity, often outweigh environmental concerns. This year, an especially severe dry season linked to El Niño has exacerbated the situation, prolonging the burning season. For Singapore and Malaysia, the haze is not just an environmental crisis but a diplomatic one, as they bear the health and economic costs of their neighbor's land-clearing practices.

pair.human_continuation: Indonesia has repeatedly said it is taking steps to prevent illegal forest burning. It has deployed troops to tackle the blazes, in Sumatra and on Indonesian Borneo, and says it is investigating 27 companies suspected of involvement in fires. But Mr Shanmugam said on Facebook: "We are hearing some shocking statements made, at senior levels, from Indonesia," noting that PSI readings had reached nearly 2,000 in parts of Indonesia.
